t: Hangzhou began as the Qin county of Qiantang, became a prefectural seat under the Sui in 589 and was joined to the north by the Grand Canal, which reached its full length by 609.
From 1132 until the Mongol conquest of 1276 it was the capital of the Southern Song as Lin'an, and its population grew far beyond its walls, with estimates of more than one million.

Under the Yuan and later dynasties it remained a commercial and administrative centre, its harbour silted up by the middle of the Ming, and the Taiping, warlords and Japanese occupation each brought damage or contest in the 19th and 20th centuries.
dyk: Hangzhou's reputation among Europeans was such that it was the intended destination of Christopher Columbus's first voyage to the Americas in 1492 and 1493.
ev: The First Emperor of the Qin establishes Qiantang as a county

f.founded: Established as the county of Qiantang by the First Emperor of the Qin, in 221 or 222 BCE; made the seat of the prefecture of Hang under the Sui in 589 CE, from which the name Hangzhou came.
f.where: At the southern end of the Grand Canal and the head of Hangzhou Bay, north of the Qiantang River and beside West Lake, in northwestern Zhejiang province, China.
f.known: The Southern Song capital Lin'an; West Lake and the causeways of Bai Juyi and Su Shi; the southern end of the Grand Canal; a population said to have made it the largest city in the world; accounts by Marco Polo, Odoric of Pordenone and Ibn Battuta; Longjing tea; the fires of the Song city
f.today: Hangzhou is the capital and most populous city of Zhejiang province and a sub-provincial city in the Yangtze River Delta.
